By 14 May 2021 (the date of last search), we identified and screened a total of 4,870 entries. After screening 204 full-text articles, 30 studies were included (Figure) [3-32]. Twenty-six studies reported on infections (irrespective of whether they were symptomatic or not), including three studies that reported both outcomes, and four additional studies reported exclusively on asymptomatic infections.

Of the 28 non-randomised studies, risk of bias was critical in four studies which did not adjust for confounders and reported unadjusted estimates. In a further two non-randomised studies, risk of bias was considered to be serious because adjustment for confounders was inappropriate. Besides one study with unclear risk of bias, all remaining studies had moderate risk of bias, mainly due to possible residual confounding (see Supplement Part S5 for details).
